scope: opt_sweep2 (Strategy Sweep 2), EXPLORATORY — not pre-registered against the trial ledger, no bar moved, nothing booked

window.train_book_window: 2011-07-01..2023-03-31 (matches OP-D6b/standing-book window, 2878 trading days, bounded by the India-VIX vault's 2023-04-05 end)
window.full_history_context: 2007-09-17..2026-04-13 (nifty50 vault) used only for the VIX-free rv_p robustness split (A3)

data_used: ingest/vault/index/nifty50_daily_2007_2026.csv (Open, Close; Adj Close verified == Close everywhere, ratio max|diff|<1e-9)
cell_breakdown: A1-A3 descriptive splits (3) + B standalone sleeve stats for 5 legs at 0bp (5) + C cost grid: 3 variants x {0,2,5,10}bp (12) + C breakeven confirmation sims (3) + D book-level baseline recompute (1) + D book-level grid: 3 variants x {0,2,5,10}bp (12) + E single-day forensics (worst-5 ranking + demonetization zoom) (2) = 38

methodology.legs: o_t = Open_t/Close_{t-1}-1 (overnight), i_t = Close_t/Open_t-1 (intraday) — identity (1+o)(1+i)-1 == Close.pct_change() verified to <1e-9, raw OHLC (no adjustment mismatch, Adj Close==Close in this vault)
methodology.gate: VIX-pct = expanding_percentile(india_vix, min_obs=252) via quant.ladder.credit_cycle — the SAME series (sd_full) the standing core already uses for its 0.90 stand-down halving; gated with an extra shift(1) so day-t's leg choice uses only info through close t-1
methodology.sizing: UNCHANGED vol-target formula: expo = (0.15/EWMA_vol_0.94).clip(upper=1.5) * (0.5 if VIX-pct>=0.90 else 1.0), same as the standing core's core_stream(). Only the RETURN LEG harvested changes across variants (full/overnight/overnight_calm/hybrid/intraday); the risk model stays close-to-close.

variants.overnight_calm: expo.shift(1) * o_t on VIX-pct(t-1)<0.60 days; FLAT (0 return, 0 trade) on VIX-pct(t-1)>=0.60 days
variants.hybrid: expo.shift(1) * o_t on VIX-pct(t-1)>=0.60 (stress) days; expo.shift(1) * full-day r_t on calm days (continuously held, no extra round trip)
variants.intraday: expo.shift(1) * i_t every day (diagnostic complement only)

methodology.cost_model: 1 round trip/day = 2 one-way legs; drag = 2*bp/1e4*expo.shift(1), charged only on days a round trip is actually incurred by that variant's construction (every day for 'overnight'; only calm days for 'overnight_calm'; only stress days for 'hybrid' — its calm days are continuously held, same as the standing core, zero extra cost)
methodology.book_substitution: monkey-patched the OP-D6b engine's module-level `core_stream` name (function objects share __globals__ with run_book since both are exec'd into one namespace — reassigning the name before calling run_book redirects it) so run_book(0.65,0.20,0.15,financing=True,syn_margin=True) — the exact OP-D6b a5 call — uses the substituted core leg while all other machinery (20% switcher, 15% factor sleeve, condor, put ladder, covered calls, financing, syn_margin) is untouched
methodology.no_lookahead: expo and gate both use only info through close t-1 (expo.shift(1), gate pre-shifted); o_t itself uses only Open_t and Close_{t-1}, both known by the point the overnight position would be entered

findings.name: A_bug_caught: realized_vol NaN-propagation trap
findings.numbers: First pass fed nf['Close'].pct_change() (leading NaN) into quant.ladder.fast_stress.realized_vol -> its cumsum-of-squares silently propagates that NaN through the ENTIRE rest of the series, so expanding_percentile on it degenerated to n=0 in the 'calm' bucket (all-NaN gate). Fixed by pre-dropping the leading NaN, exactly as scripts/analyze_t1b_t6.py's T1b already does (`rets_clean = df.dropna(subset=['ret'])`) before calling the same function.
findings.method: adversarial self-check: an n=0 conditional bucket was the tell; traced to numpy cumsum's NaN-forward-propagation.
findings.lookahead_risk: none (a correctness bug, not a lookahead) — flagged because quant/stats machinery is supposed to be reused as-is (process note #6); this is a real, reproducible footgun in quant/ladder/fast_stress.py.realized_vol worth a note to whoever next calls it on an un-cleaned returns series.

findings.name: A1/A2/A3: overnight/intraday decomposition reproduces T1 doctrine, but the SIGN of the stress-day overnight print is gate-dependent
findings.numbers: Book window (2011-07..2023-03) unconditional: overnight +29.72%/yr (NW t=+9.22), intraday -18.31%/yr (t=-4.79). VIX-pct split: calm (n=2000) overnight +24.69%/yr (matches the booked +24%/yr T1 headline almost exactly) vs stress (n=878) overnight +41.18%/yr (t=+4.82) — HIGHER in the VIX-pct-defined stress bucket, not lower. Full-history (2007-2026) rv_p split (T1b's own gate): calm (n=4196) overnight +25.10%/yr vs stress (n=357) overnight +11.40%/yr (t=+0.87, not significant) — weaker but still positive; intraday degrades much more sharply under this gate (-10.41%/yr calm vs -38.26%/yr stress).
findings.method: Newey-West (5-lag) t-stats on daily leg means, annualized x252, house convention from scripts/analyze_t1_overnight.py.
findings.lookahead_risk: none (both gates pre-shifted). But the VIX-pct-vs-rv_p sign flip on the stress bucket is a real fragility: VIX-pct is slower/stickier (stays elevated deep into a post-crash rally) while rv_p(21d) is more contemporaneous — this repo's own C07 already documented VIX-pct-adjacent buckets getting contaminated by post-crash REBOUND days (F07/F09, 2.16x enrichment). The same mechanism likely explains why 'VIX-pct stress' shows a strong positive overnight mean here: it is plausibly capturing rebound-day gaps-up, not genuine ongoing-crisis nights. Not independently re-verified with an episode exclusion in this pass — flagged, not resolved.

findings.name: B: standalone sleeve stats (vol-target sized, no cost, core-only, no overlays)
findings.numbers: full-day (baseline): CAGR +7.17%/yr, vol 14.80%, Sharpe +0.55, maxDD -26.09%, worst yr -9.4%. overnight (unconditional): CAGR +31.16%/yr, vol 8.32%, Sharpe +3.41, maxDD -8.72%, worst yr +6.0%. overnight_calm: CAGR +20.94%/yr, vol 7.03%, Sharpe +2.82, maxDD -8.87%, worst yr +2.8%. hybrid: CAGR +12.18%/yr, vol 13.41%, Sharpe +0.95, maxDD -23.31%, worst yr -7.4%. intraday (diagnostic): CAGR -19.03%/yr, maxDD -91.85%.
findings.method: same vol-target expo(cap=1.5, financing=True) applied to each leg; CAGR/maxDD from stats_of() on the resulting equity curve; this is the CORE SLEEVE ALONE (100% weight, no put ladder / covered calls / other sleeves) — NOT comparable in level to the 65%-weighted, overlay-hedged whole book (section D).
findings.lookahead_risk: none — but the eye-catching Sharpe 3.41 for unconditional overnight is a symptom, not a free lunch: see E1/E2 and the cost-breakeven finding below.

findings.name: C: cost breakeven vs the standing (uncosted) full-day core is very low — ~3-4bp one-way
findings.numbers: Interpolated one-way breakeven bp (where the variant's standalone CAGR = the full-day core's costless +7.17%/yr): overnight 4.3bp (confirmed CAGR +5.27%/yr, still 1.9pp short at the interpolated point because CAGR-vs-bp is not perfectly linear — the confirmation run at 4.3bp landed 1.9pp BELOW target, meaning the TRUE breakeven is lower than 4.3bp, closer to ~3bp); overnight_calm 3.2bp (confirmed CAGR +6.24%/yr, 0.93pp short, true breakeven also somewhat under 3.2bp); hybrid 4.4bp (confirmed CAGR +7.09%/yr, only 0.08pp short — closest to linear, true breakeven ~4.5bp). Registered grid: at 2bp ALL THREE variants still beat the full-day core; at 5bp ALL THREE variants lose to it; the crossover sits inside [2,5]bp for every variant.
findings.method: 4-point grid at {0,2,5,10}bp one-way, cost = 2*bp/1e4*expo(t-1) charged on active-round-trip days only; breakeven from a linear fit across the 4 points then confirmed by direct resimulation at the fitted bp (the confirmation runs show the true fit is CONCAVE in this range, i.e. cost drag compounds faster than linear once volatility-driven exposure swings interact with daily rebalancing drag — so the linear-fit breakevens above are mild OVERESTIMATES of the true one-way cost this design can survive).
findings.lookahead_risk: none. Caveat: no cost model here includes India F&O-specific frictions (STT on futures ~2bp one-way on the sell leg, exchange/SEBI turnover fees, stamp duty, GST on brokerage, and market impact for institutional size trading the FULL exposure notional twice a day, every day, for 12 years) — a realistic all-in Indian index-derivative cost stack for this much daily churn plausibly SITS AT OR ABOVE the ~2-4bp breakeven found here, which is why this is reported as a caveat rather than resolved with a specific principal-machine cost number (not vaulted; no live cost feed in this environment).

findings.name: D: book-level substitution (65/20/15 weights) — same breakeven pattern reproduces at the whole-book level
findings.numbers: Recomputed full-day baseline (this script's own plumbing): CAGR +11.13%/yr, maxDD -11.53%, worst yr -2.3% — EXACT match to the booked OP-D6b a5 numbers (+11.13/-11.53/-2.3), confirming the monkey-patch preserves the untouched machinery correctly. Gross (0bp): overnight +26.31%/yr (+15.18pp) maxDD -5.50% (+6.03pp); overnight_calm +19.71%/yr (+8.58pp) maxDD -6.85% (+4.68pp); hybrid +14.36%/yr (+3.23pp) maxDD -9.43% (+2.10pp). At 2bp: all three STILL beat the baseline (overnight +18.23, overnight_calm +13.62, hybrid +12.81, vs +11.13 baseline). At 5bp: overnight (+7.07%/yr, -4.06pp) and overnight_calm (+5.06%/yr, -6.07pp) both fall BELOW the baseline; hybrid is marginal (+10.52%/yr, -0.61pp, essentially tied). Book-level hybrid breakeven interpolates to ~4.2bp — consistent with the ~4.4bp standalone-sleeve breakeven, a useful cross-check that the result is not an artifact of which level (sleeve vs whole book) it's measured at. At 10bp all three variants are well below baseline, and 'overnight'/'overnight_calm' at 10bp show catastrophic maxDD (-70%/-66%) because the daily round-trip drag compounds against a book that is also carrying the condor+put-ladder overlays sized off the SAME (now cost-eroded) core notional.
findings.method: core_stream monkey-patch into the exact OP-D6b a5 run_book(0.65,0.20,0.15,financing=True,syn_margin=True) call; stats_of() on the resulting book equity curve.
findings.lookahead_risk: none. The 10bp maxDD blow-up (-70%/-66%) is itself informative: it shows the design has a POSITIVE FEEDBACK failure mode once daily cost drag turns the core sleeve's own compounding negative — a real fragility of any daily-round-trip sleeve sitting inside a levered, overlay-heavy book, not a lookahead artifact.

findings.name: E: single-day forensics — the mechanism behind the small maxDD is COVID-specific, and the same design lost MORE than the standing core on a real, different, non-vol-preceded shock
findings.numbers: Worst 5 standalone-overnight-sleeve days: 2016-11-09 demonetization -7.26% of book (expo_lag 1.304x, o_t -5.57%); 2018-02-06 -4.21% (expo_lag 1.209x); 2020-02-03 -3.82%; 2016-06-24 Brexit -3.62%; 2015-08-24 China deval -3.15%. On 2016-11-09 specifically: overnight -5.57% (captured IN FULL by overnight-only, -7.26% of book at 1.304x exposure) vs intraday +4.52% (the SAME-DAY partial recovery, captured ONLY by full-day exposure) vs full-day net -1.31% (only -1.70% of book at the same exposure). The overnight-only design lost 4.3x MORE of book on this single night than the full-day core would have. Context: by 2020-03-23 (COVID low) exposure had already de-risked to 0.13x (from 1.10-1.15x on 2020-02-17..24) because the preceding 3-4 weeks of rising realized vol had already fed through the EWMA sizing BEFORE the worst single-day gap landed — that gradual-onset luck is why COVID does not dominate the overnight sleeve's maxDD, but demonetization (a surprise policy shock with zero vol runway) still does.
findings.method: direct point lookups of expo_lag, o_t, i_t, full-day return on named dates from the same series used throughout.
findings.lookahead_risk: none — this is exactly the CONTRACT §7 known-prior #8 concern ('fast crashes cannot be met by cycles... a five-week 38% fall with no prior signal, no') reproduced concretely for this specific family: overnight-only removes the exact session (intraday) in which an overreacting gap gets partially reversed, and adds NO protection against a shock that arrives with no vol runway. It is not merely 'less bad on average' during stress (per A2/A3's fragile positive stress-mean) — it can be mechanically WORSE than the status quo on the single worst class of event this book is explicitly built to survive.

why: Gross/uncosted, this family looks spectacular (book-level CAGR +26.3%/yr at -5.5% maxDD vs the standing +11.1%/-11.5%) — but that headline is exactly the shape CONTRACT §5 (governing principle: assume your alpha decays) warns against taking at face value: a return that requires 2 fresh one-way trades on the FULL core notional every single trading day, for 12 years, with no capacity limit, no institutional-constraint story, and no structural reason a well-capitalized counterparty would keep paying it. This sweep's own cost-breakeven cells put the survivable one-way cost at roughly 2-4bp before the edge inverts, at BOTH the standalone-sleeve and whole-book level (a genuine cross-check, not just one lucky cut), and the confirmation resimulations show the true breakeven is a shade BELOW even the linear-fit estimate. A realistic all-in Indian index-derivative cost stack for this much daily churn (STT, exchange/SEBI fees, stamp duty, brokerage GST, plus market impact at the aggressive/moderate/conservative book sizes named in the mandate) plausibly sits at or above that threshold -- this is a caveat, not a resolved number, because no live cost feed is available in this environment (principal-machine item). Two further findings undercut confidence in even the LEAST aggressive (hybrid) variant: (1) the calm/stress conditional mean FLIPS SIGN depending on which gate is used (VIX-pct says stress-day overnight is stronger; the VIX-free rv_p gate says it is weaker and marginal), and the VIX-pct read is the more suspect one given this program's own documented rebound-day contamination pattern (C07); (2) the single worst realistic tail event examined in detail (2016 demonetization, a genuine zero-warning policy shock) shows overnight-only losing 4.3x MORE of book than the standing full-day core on that exact night, because it structurally forfeits the SAME-DAY intraday reversal that cushioned the full-day core -- the opposite of the COVID case, where weeks of vol runway had already de-risked the position before the worst print. Net: this is a clean negative for a CORE REPLACEMENT at any of the three tested designs (unconditional, calm-gated, hybrid) under real transaction frictions, and even at zero cost the mechanism is fragile (gate-dependent sign, one bad-shock-night counterexample already found in-sample without searching for it). It duplicates none of the standing book's other sleeves' exposure (it IS the core, just re-timed), so there's no overlap concern -- the objection is cost survivability and tail-mechanism fragility, not redundancy.

proposed_design.rule: NOT PROMOTED. If the principal wants this pursued further (e.g. because desk execution costs on NIFTY futures are confirmed sub-1.5bp all-in for this book's size), the ONLY variant worth a pre-registered trial is the HYBRID (overnight-only when VIX-pct(t-1)>=0.60, full-day otherwise) -- it needs the fewest extra round trips (active only ~30% of days, n=878/2878 in this window), has the smallest gross CAGR add (+3.2pp) and smallest gross maxDD improvement (+2.1pp) to lose if costs eat it, and does not touch calm-day compounding at all. Do NOT promote unconditional or calm-gated overnight-only under any cost assumption tested -- both cross to a loss below the middle of the required {2,5,10}bp reporting grid.
proposed_design.frozen_params: IF re-opened as its own pre-registered design (not done here): threshold VIX-pct>=0.60 (reuses the existing config/ladder.yaml L2 grid point, not a new magic number), stress-day leg = overnight only (o_t = Open_t/Close_{t-1}-1), calm-day leg = full-day (unchanged), same expo=(0.15/EWMA_0.94_vol).clip(1.5)*stand-down-halving sizing as today's core, cost assumption to be SUPPLIED by the principal-machine execution-cost pull (RUNSHEET item, not vaulted) before any bar is set -- this family cannot pre-register a numeric bar for itself without that number.
proposed_design.confidence: low -- the honest expectation, pending a real cost number, is that the add nets to ~0 (breakeven sits inside the family's own required cost-reporting grid), not the gross +3.2pp shown at 0bp; DD impact is likewise expected to wash out once daily-drag effects on a levered, overlay-carrying book (section D's 10bp blow-up) are counted. Reported as 0.0/0.0 rather than the gross numbers because presenting the gross figures as 'expected' would misstate a result this sweep itself shows is almost entirely a transaction-cost artifact.

caveats: India VIX vault ends 2023-04-05; no 2008 GFC in the VIX-conditioned split (A2, D); a genuinely 2008-style crash's overnight/intraday split under this design is untested (OP-D2 SYNTHESIS caveat #1, same environment).

Post-2023-04 tail missing (743+ days, including the 2024 election spike and SEBI 2024-26 derivatives curbs, breaks-registry C2) -- daily-round-trip microstructure costs may have shifted materially under the curbs; this family's cost-breakeven numbers are pre-curb.

No cost model beyond a flat bp-per-round-trip proxy: no bid-ask/impact curve by size, no STT/exchange-fee/stamp-duty/GST stack, no distinction between cash-index vs futures execution. Real Indian F&O costs for this much daily churn are a principal-machine item, not resolved here.

Financing (6%/yr on expo>1x) held IDENTICAL across all variants (full-day and overnight-only) -- a modeling assumption (borrowed capital is outstanding overnight either way) that was not itself tested for sensitivity.
Price-only index (booked +1.3pp TR note applies uniformly here too; not separately re-derived for these variants since it affects the numerator equally across the comparison).

The book-level results (section D) still carry the put-ladder/covered-call/condor overlay machinery UNCHANGED and sized off the SAME core notional/exposure formula as the standing book -- overlay behavior under an overnight-only core was not independently re-examined (e.g. whether the covered-call notional or put ladder still makes sense when the underlying core no longer holds intraday exposure).

A2's VIX-pct stress-day finding (overnight premium HIGHER, not lower, under stress) is flagged but not resolved with an episode-exclusion re-run in this pass -- a natural follow-up cell if this family is ever reopened.
